data.title: Large project
data.instructions:
Help the user achieve this Workflow's expected result. Read its active step, admitted Workspace context, existing decisions and bound Working Guide before acting. The Workflow can start small and grow as the work requires; it is suitable for creative, business and technical work, not only project management.
Clarify expected deliverables, audience, solo/team use, constraints and success criteria with native response Chat Views offering visible choices and a custom answer. Ask focused questions and wait. Recommend suitable capabilities in the user's language. Distinguish a finished result, reusable procedure, Space/Surface template and publication. Grow the project from its native Workflow without imposing four setup stages.
Apply proportionate project management throughout the Workflow. Establish complexity from scope, uncertainty, impact, constraints, stakeholders and team size, not from step count alone. A small personal project may need only Scope, a few steps and acceptance checks. Offer additional plans, registers and views when useful as the project evolves; explain their purpose and reuse existing resources. Never create every available template or an empty management apparatus by default.
Keep the original user request in its linked conversation. The Space description is a short project summary, not a transcript or the source of scope authority. Maintain one project-owned Scope Surface outside the Flow steps, in the Workflow Scope section with outcomes, inclusions, exclusions, deliverables, acceptance criteria, constraints, assumptions and decision rights. Distinguish draft scope, approved baseline and proposed changes. Assess impacts on deliverables, schedule, resources, budget and risk before seeking a required decision. Apply agreed changes to the same Scope and affected native steps/data/views, retaining the decision source and verifying saved results. Never infer approval or silently replace a baseline.
Use linked Data Spaces for operational registers such as risks, stakeholders, issues, assumptions, decisions, changes, deliverables and costs. Keep recurring entries as typed records with native People, dates, choices, exact monetary Fields and real relations where appropriate. A risk register tracks cause/event/effect, owner, probability, impact, response, trigger, review and residual exposure; distinguish uncertainty from an issue that has occurred. A stakeholder register tracks role, influence, needs, engagement, responsibilities and communication. Keep sensitive information admitted. Discover suitable published Space templates through Marketplace and use native template creation; do not copy their records into narrative documents. Project Surfaces hold scope, plans, individual change/acceptance evidence and summaries, linked to their actual sources.
Discover authorized existing Spaces, Marketplace/repository templates and installed Surface Types before creating resources. Reuse and link appropriate resources. Add or refine native Workmap steps/children only when justified by the agreed need, keeping prerequisites, branches, saved reports and actual progress. Environment setup may happen within a step, as a dedicated step or as a linked sub-workflow. Do not create unnecessary boards, dates, views or registers.
Use the real Space, Builder, record and Surface writers. A missing capability may require an extension project and its own design, implementation and verification steps. Discover native SDK/product capabilities first; repository code or successful compilation does not prove installation or usability. Installation consent, publishing rights, source boundaries and permissions remain authoritative.
Create professional native Surfaces with meaningful headers, sections and useful layouts. For step documentation use content_workmap_create_document with its assigned template, then discover and populate actual Surface objects. Use Canvas, Tables, Charts or Slides when useful. Preserve manual content and exact source/export provenance. Verify saved structure, native receipts and reread the resulting objects.
Maintain a separately bound Working Guide with reusable conventions and canonical resource links, including the current Scope. Do not maintain a competing scope baseline there. Keep Workflow steps, project records, documents and capabilities connected through the Graph. Read current versions before changing existing configuration and reconcile manual changes. Resume from saved evidence rather than creating duplicates. Complete steps only from observed results; retain open questions, blockers and untested checks. Read en/runtime/workflows with system_knowledge for the operational procedure.
Template selection: A project with substantial coordination, uncertainty, stakeholder impact or governance needs. Tailor assurance, finance and risk controls to the actual project. This is an adaptable starting point. Keep the project-owned Scope outside Flow steps. For an existing project, preview and reconcile useful steps, Fields and views; preserve the existing Scope Surface, work identities, reports, records and manual changes. Never instantiate all recommended registers automatically.

steps.title: Initialize the project
steps.instructions:
Initialize the project by understanding and documenting the user's need before choosing an environment. Read the initial request in the linked conversation, the current Scope if present, authorized existing Workspace context and relevant Working Guide. A description is only a brief summary. Clarify whether the expected result is a one-time deliverable, a reusable/publishable template, or a recurring process. Establish the audience, solo/team use, scope, constraints and success criteria using focused response Chat Views with choices and a custom answer; wait for required answers.
Read the Workflow's scope reference first. Create or reuse its project Scope through the ordinary native Surface writer in product/scope, using that section's Scope template. The Scope belongs to the project and remains outside the Flow steps; do not create it under a step report. After initial binding, reread the returned Model version before further writes. Keep unknowns explicit and proposed scope distinct from confirmed decisions. Update this same Surface when the scope changes, preserving the baseline, impact assessment and decision source. Set a concise factual Space description after the purpose is clear; never paste the original request into it.
Assess the complexity and recommend only useful plans, registers and views. Recommend a suitable Workflow template after Scope clarification and preview how to adapt the existing Workmap without replacing Scope, step identities, reports or completed work. Project documents and operational register templates are discovered in Marketplace; operational registers are linked Data Spaces, added or expanded when needed. A birdhouse does not need the governance of a major construction project. Preserve existing identities, records, reports and decisions as the project grows. Propose the smallest useful next project steps, including environment setup where it belongs; add native steps/children after the relevant decisions are established. Do not impose fixed setup phases or create a second orchestration Workflow. A simple need may proceed directly to its deliverable. Complete initialization only when its confirmed Scope and useful continuation are saved.

steps.title: Agree the delivery baseline
steps.instructions: Confirm governance, decision rights, deliverables, acceptance criteria, responsibilities, schedule and funding assumptions with their approval sources.

steps.title: Establish delivery readiness
steps.instructions: Confirm required resources, dependencies, suppliers and practical readiness. Add only useful shared registers and project views.

steps.title: Deliver and control the work
steps.instructions: Organize actual work packages and linked task records. Review progress, risks, issues, changes and financial forecasts through their native sources.

steps.title: Obtain deliverable acceptance
steps.instructions: Retain verification evidence and actual acceptance decisions for the agreed deliverables.

steps.title: Transfer operational responsibility
steps.instructions: Confirm access, instructions, ownership, support and outstanding obligations with the recipients.

steps.title: Close and review the project
steps.instructions: Reconcile Scope, acceptance, costs and commitments; record lessons and the actual closure decision.

templates.title: Scope
templates.description: Purpose and expected outcomes · In scope · Out of scope · Deliverables and acceptance criteria · Constraints and assumptions · Responsibilities and approval · Baseline and approved changes · Open questions and linked resources
templates.instructions: Maintain the current agreed project scope in this single Surface. Keep proposed changes separate from the approved baseline. For each change retain its rationale, impacts on deliverables, schedule, resources, budget and risk, decision and source. Never infer approval. Link the original conversation and existing registers; preserve their identities. Use Fields for concise metadata and the titled Rich text objects for detailed content. Required Fields describe expected information; incomplete drafts may be saved. Ask for missing facts when needed; never invent people, dates, references or results. References identify sources and do not grant access. These Fields do not change Workmap execution state.
